model: probability-weighted scenario model on forward EV/Sales exit with explicit per-scenario dilution (NOT a discounted-FCF model)
valuation_philosophy: TruScreen straddles the 'operating company' and 'distressed' rows of the dcf-methods routing table. It is a going concern with real, audited revenue (NZ$2.43m FY2026, +42%, sold into ~10 countries) and a validated product (COGA 14,982-patient study, BMC Cancer Feb-2026), so a receivership/creditor waterfall is wrong. But it has lost money in all ten fiscal years on record (FY2017-FY2026), owner FCF is negative in every one of them (FY2026 -NZ$2.64m), the auditor's FY2026 report carries a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph, and every year's burn has been refilled by a placement at a lower price (NZ$0.022 May-2025 -> NZ$0.013-0.014 May-2026), taking the share count from 364m (FY2023) to 1,048m (Aug-2026). An owner-FCF DCF has no positive flow to discount and Gordon math on negative flows is meaningless; a book-value model is meaningless because intangibles are fully impaired and NTA is simply the last raise's cash minus burn. The model used instead: three scenarios valued on a forward (FY2029E) EV/Sales exit appropriate to each path, each with its own funding path - option exercise, a further discounted raise, or a wind-down - modelled explicitly through the scenario's diluted share count and cash at exit, discounted 2.5 years at a 25% NZD cost of equity. Wind-down is priced as an explicit 50%-weighted branch inside a 35%-weighted bear scenario, NOT in the discount rate, so survival risk is charged exactly once. The weighted IV of NZ$0.0081 sits ~46% below the NZ$0.015 price. The finding, stated plainly: today's NZ$15.7m market cap (4.9x trailing sales for a 31.5%-gross-margin business burning NZ$2.5m a year) is only recoverable if the bull path - a UNITAID/NGO programme win in Nov-2026 plus China consumables finally growing plus all 316m options exercising - is treated as roughly two-thirds likely. The filings do not support that weighting yet.

inputs.net_cash_estimate_note: Cash is an ESTIMATE as at ~mid-Sep-2026, not a balance-sheet figure: 31-Mar-2026 audited cash NZ$1.463m + May-Aug-2026 raise gross NZ$4.034m (placement 128.74m sh @0.014 + rights 149.46m sh @0.013 + oversubscriptions 22.19m sh @0.013, per NZX announcements 473006/475060/477288) less ~9% cash raise costs (FY2026 precedent 9.4%) = net NZ$3.671m, less 5.5 months of burn at the FY2026 run-rate (OCF -2.471 + lease principal -0.121 = NZ$0.216m/month) = NZ$3.95m. Treat as +/-NZ$0.5m: the FY2026 year-end trade receivable of NZ$1.03m (up from NZ$0.02m - a single distributor on extended terms) may or may not have collected. total_debt NZ$0.201m is IFRS-16 lease liabilities only (no borrowings) and is EXCLUDED from net debt under lease treatment (B). The H1 FY2027 interim (due ~Nov/Dec 2026) is the refresh trigger.
inputs.lease_treatment: B - lease payments deducted inside cash overheads (and lease principal deducted from historical owner FCF); lease liabilities excluded from net debt

inputs.notes: Model: probability-weighted scenario model on a forward EV/Sales exit with explicit per-scenario dilution, per the dcf-methods routing for a name straddling the distressed and operating-company rows (precedents in this folder: RUA.NZ, MEE.NZ). Owner-FCF DCF rejected: no positive owner FCF in any of ten periods, so there is nothing to capitalise and Gordon on a negative flow runs away. NTA/book rejected: intangibles fully impaired, NTA = last raise minus burn (~NZ$0.005/share). Receivership waterfall rejected: going-concern basis, audited unqualified opinion with a material-uncertainty paragraph, real growing revenue. Deal-weighting not applicable: no live corporate action. First valuation of this ticker - no MEMORY.md entry existed. Filings are in WHOLE NZD (rounded to the nearest dollar); CSV in millions; EPS in dollars. Reporting and quote currency are both NZD (the company also lists on ASX; the ASX quote is in AUD but the NZX quote used here is NZD). Lease treatment (B). Risk charged once: survival risk sits in the scenario weights and the bear's wind-down branch; the 25% cost of equity carries size, illiquidity and execution risk within a surviving-company path, not a second survival premium. IMPORTANT for the dashboard: this JSON does not carry owner-FCF component drivers (ebitda_margin_path / da_pct / capex_pct / cash_tax_rate_path) because the valuation is not produced by that engine; the component slider engine should fall back and the scenario table should be read from valuation[*].

wacc_rationale: 25% NZD cost of equity (there is no debt, so WACC = CoE). Built from the flows' own currency: NZ 10-yr government ~4.3% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.5 = ~12.5% for a listed NZ small-cap, plus ~12.5pp for a NZ$16m nano-cap with 1,914 holders, thin liquidity (many days trade at one tick), single-product/single-market (China 61%) concentration and a going-concern-qualified balance sheet - the range venture investors apply to a revenue-stage medtech that has not yet shown operating leverage. Folder precedent: RUA.NZ 28%, 2CC.NZ 19%. The rate is applied identically to all three scenarios (section 7f: no per-scenario discount-rate differences); survival risk is in the weights, not the rate.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+0.6%/3yr, -25.5%/5yr) diverges from revenue CAGR (+13.6%/3yr, +16.5%/5yr) by far more than 30%, but neither is a usable anchor: equity is raised cash minus burn (every year's loss is refilled by a placement), so its CAGR measures the raise cadence, not compounding; FCF and EPS CAGRs are undefined because owner FCF and EPS are negative in all ten periods on record. Revenue CAGR is the only real series and it is distorted at both ends: FY2023-FY2025 was flat-to-down (1.66 -> 2.11 -> 1.71) and the FY2026 +42% was device placements - the recurring consumable (SUS) line grew 1% (ASM deck, 1-Sep-2026). The selected 25.4% is the BASE scenario's forward revenue CAGR, used only as the screener's forward-growth proxy.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF history (reported FCF - SBC - interest income - IFRS-16 lease principal) is negative in every year FY2017-FY2026; FY2026 owner FCF NZ$-2.635m vs reported NZ$-2.471m. Loss per share has narrowed (-0.0066 -> -0.0032 over 3 years) purely because the share count rose 364m -> 701m weighted; the dollar loss was flat at ~NZ$2.2-2.4m.

base.narrative: Revenue grows ~25%/yr off the FY2026 base: the deferred Zimbabwe 10,000-SUS order and the Uzbekistan pilot land in FY2027, India registration (guided 3-6 months from Jun-2026) opens a first commercial year in FY2028, the Vietnam HCMC 260,000-women programme ramps slowly, and China consumables grow modestly (SUS +1% in FY2026). No UNITAID win, or a win too small/late to matter inside the horizon. Gross margin improves 31.5% -> 37% as management guides ('expected to further improve in FY2027'). Cash overheads rise 4%/yr from the FY2026 NZ$3.36m because management is explicit that market development requires investment. Receivables absorb 20% of each year's revenue increase (FY2026 saw a NZ$1.0m receivable build on NZ$0.7m of growth). Cumulative FY2027-29 burn ~NZ$6.1m against NZ$5.1m pro-forma cash, so ONE further raise is modelled in FY2028: NZ$3.0m gross at NZ$0.010 (+300m shares), consistent with the annual raise cadence and each raise printing below the last (0.022 -> 0.014 -> 0.010). The NZ$0.022 TRUOD options lapse Jul-2027 and the 0.014/0.019 tranches lapse Aug-2028. Exit at 2.5x FY2029E sales - a multiple for a sub-scale, still-loss-making, distributor-led device company facing another raise, NOT the 4-5x the market has paid TRU on the story. Net cash at exit ~NZ$1.8m.

bull.narrative: The Nov-2026 UNITAID decision delivers at least one of the five applications TruScreen is technology partner in (company: 'may add NZ$4m to annual revenue from FY2028 to FY2030'), the CSCCP Expert Consensus in China opens public-programme procurement so consumables finally compound, and the Vietnam/Zimbabwe/India programmes convert: FY2027E NZ$3.6m -> FY2028E NZ$6.5m -> FY2029E NZ$10.0m, gross margin 35% -> 44% on programme SUS volume. Overheads scale to NZ$4.9m. The share price re-rates above NZ$0.022 on the UNITAID news, so all 316.2m options exercise (NZ$6.18m: TRUOD in FY2028, TRUOE/TRUOF in FY2029) and NO discounted raise is needed; dilution stops at 1,364.0m. Approaching operating breakeven in FY2029 with ~NZ$6.4m net cash. Exit at 4.5x FY2029E sales - a growing, near-breakeven medtech with public-screening contracts, about the multiple the market pays TRU today. This is the scenario the current price needs to be ~two-thirds likely.
bull.options_exercised: all: TRUOD 204.69m @0.022 (FY2028), TRUOE 89.05m @0.014 and TRUOF 22.5m @0.019 (FY2029); proceeds NZ$6.18m

bear.narrative: China (61% of sales) softens - the NZ$1.03m year-end trade receivable from a distributor on extended terms signals channel stuffing or a struggling partner - and the new markets repeat FY2026's pattern of orders slipping (Uzbekistan awaiting payment, Zimbabwe deferred): revenue FY2027E NZ$2.2m, flat thereafter, gross margin stuck at 31%. Overheads are cut to NZ$2.8m but the business still burns ~NZ$1.8m/yr, so cash (NZ$5.1m pro forma) runs out during FY2029 with no growth story to raise against; all options lapse. Two branches, 50/50: (i) wind-down / failed raise - ~NZ$1.2m cash entering FY2029 less ~NZ$0.8m of wind-down costs plus ~NZ$0.5m for the IP and registrations sold to a distributor = ~NZ$0.9m to 1,047.7m shares = NZ$0.0009 (PV NZ$0.0005); (ii) punitive recap - NZ$2.5m gross at NZ$0.005 (+500m shares -> 1,547.7m), exit at 1.0x FY2029E sales of NZ$2.4m plus ~NZ$1.8m cash = NZ$0.0027/share (PV NZ$0.0016). Blended bear IV NZ$0.0010 - a ~93% loss from NZ$0.015.

base.terminal_value_bound: exit multiple (no Gordon in this model)

bear.implied_exit_multiple_basis: EV/Sales on FY2029E revenue, recap branch; wind-down branch is a recovery value

valuation.notes: terminal_pct_of_value is 100% by construction: all value is the discounted exit value, there are no positive interim flows. street = house in every scenario: the model is not FCF-based so the SBC accounting-regime band does not operate; SBC is NZ$0.04m (1.5% of revenue) and dilution is charged explicitly through scenario share counts instead. The bear scenario's wind-down branch is the analogue of a scenario hitting the terminal-value floor: it says the business does not survive that path, which is a finding.

no_rerate_reference.note: Memo, not a replacement: base-case revenue and dilution path with the exit multiple held at TODAY'S 4.83x EV/trailing sales instead of 2.5x. Even granting the market's own multiple, the base case is worth NZ$0.0106 - below the NZ$0.015 price - because the modelled FY2028 raise dilutes the count 29% and 2.5 years at 25% cost 43% of the exit value. The gap between NZ$0.0059 and NZ$0.0106 is the price of the de-rating assumption; the gap to NZ$0.015 is the price of dilution and time.

entry_price.method: Repo-standard semantics adapted to the scenario-exit model: entry price = the price at which the scenario's exit equity value per (scenario-diluted) share, discounted 2.5 years at the 15% hurdle instead of the 25% cost of equity, is recovered. No interim distributions exist to add. The exit value is the same multiple-based value in both cases (an exit multiple, not a Gordon value, so there is no WACC-built terminal value to re-derive at the hurdle). NOTE: the weighted entry price (NZ$0.0100) sits ABOVE the weighted IV (NZ$0.0081) - expected and correct here, because the 15% hurdle is far below the 25% risk-appropriate rate. The IV answers 'what is it worth at a rate that prices a surviving nano-cap's risks'; the entry price answers 'what could you pay and still make 15% in expectation'. Both are well below the current NZ$0.015.

bear.note: blend of wind-down recovery and recap branch, each discounted at 15%

required_return_table.note: 25% row is the model's own cost of equity and equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value; the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price. Even at a 9% required return the base case is worth NZ$0.0083 - 45% below the current price. The price is not explicable by discount-rate choice; it requires the bull revenue/multiple path with no further dilution.

sensitivity.axis_note: Rows: cost of equity (%). Columns: exit EV/Sales multiple on FY2029E base-case revenue of NZ$4.8m, exit net cash NZ$1.80m, 1347.7m diluted shares, 2.5-year discount. Replaces the WACC x terminal-growth grid, which does not exist in a multiple-exit model. wacc_range is the CoE axis; terminal_growth_range is null.
sensitivity.reading: The current NZ$0.015 is reached only at ~6.3x FY2029E sales at a 20% discount rate - i.e. the market is paying, on the base revenue path, a higher forward multiple than it pays today on trailing sales, while ignoring the dilution of the next raise.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 35% (vs 15% house default): the FY2026 audit report carries a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph, the directors' twelve-month forecast explicitly 'assumes revenue growth from a number of markets' that the auditor could not corroborate, China is 61% of sales with a NZ$1.03m receivable on extended terms, the recurring consumable line grew 1% in a +42% year, FY2026 guidance was cut once already, and the company has been 'about to scale' since listing (revenue NZ$0.6m FY2017 -> NZ$2.4m FY2026, with a placement at a lower price nearly every year). Bull 25% (vs 35% default): there IS a dated, real catalyst - the UNITAID decision ~Nov-2026 on five applications TruScreen is technology partner in, plus the CSCCP Expert Consensus in China and Vietnam/Zimbabwe/India programmes - which is why bull is not cut further; but the bull needs three independent things (a programme win, China consumables compounding, and a share price above NZ$0.022 by Jul-2027 so the options fund the growth) and the company's ten-year record is of announced programmes converting slowly. Base 40% carries the remainder. Weights sum to 1.0.
probability_weighted.band_note: band_position null: house and street coincide because the model is multiple-based, not FCF-based - the SBC accounting-regime band does not operate. Dilution risk is charged through explicit scenario share counts instead.
probability_weighted.verdict: Weighted IV NZ$0.0081 is ~46% BELOW the current NZ$0.015 price. Stated plainly: at these weights the stock is materially overvalued. The current price is approximately the probability-weighted value at weights of roughly bear 15% / base 22% / bull 63% - i.e. the market is treating a UNITAID/NGO programme win and option-funded growth as close to the median outcome. That is a legitimate bet on a Nov-2026 binary, but it is not what the filings support, and the downside if it fails is another sub-NZ$0.01 raise. No buy signal has been reverse-engineered: the honest answer is below the price at every discount rate in the required-return table.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

risks_priced: Going-concern material uncertainty (FY2026 audit report) - in the 35% bear weight and its 50% wind-down branch
Serial dilution at declining prices (0.022 -> 0.014 -> modelled 0.010 / 0.005) - explicit per-scenario share counts
China concentration (61% of sales) and the NZ$1.03m year-end receivable on extended terms - bear revenue path
Recurring consumable (SUS) sales +1% in FY2026 despite +42% headline - base growth held to ~25% not 42%
UNITAID Nov-2026 decision - the bull path; explicitly NOT in base
316.2m options: funding in bull, overhang in base/bear - modelled as exercise-or-lapse per scenario
Illiquidity / one-tick trading - in the 25% cost of equity
